scenes.sub: Explain why a concentrated liquidity position and a grid bot are economically close cousins, and where they differ.

scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: How it trades, Discrete orders at set levels, Continuous. Every trade in range moves your inventory. What it earns, Spread between grid levels, minus exchange fees, Share of the pool's swap fee on every trade in range. Who pays whom, You pay trading fees, Traders pay you fees. At the range low, Holds mostly/all the base asset, Holds 100% of the base asset. At the range high, Holds mostly/all quote (U.S.D.T./U.S.D.C.), Holds 100% of the quote asset. Outside the range, Stops trading, holding one side, Stops earning, holding one side. Custody, Exchange holds funds (you keep API control), You hold keys, and the contract holds the position. Main extra risk, Exchange / counterparty, Smart contract, oracle, M.E.V., gas. Automation, Built into the tool, Manual, or a third-party manager (extra contract risk).

scenes.sub: Both strategies do the same basic thing inside a price range: sell as price rises, buy as price falls, and profit from price moving back and forth.

scenes.vo: Here's the picture: Grid bot versus concentrated L.P..

scenes.title: Worked example — same range, same inventory behaviour
scenes.vo: Range $2,700–$3,300, ETH at $3,000. Price falls to $2,700: geometric average the square root of (2,700 times 3,000) about $2,846. Price rises to $3,300: Almost the same inventory path. The real difference is how money is made on the way: grid profit per completed level (after paying fees), versus L.P. fee income on all trading volume in range (after impermanent loss). Grid (20 arithmetic levels, $30 apart): buys at 2,970, 2,940 … 2,700 to average buy about $2,835. Concentrated L.P.: converts U.S.D.C. to ETH continuously on the way down at the Grid: sells at 3,030 … 3,300 to average about $3,165. L.P.: sells ETH at the square root of (3,000 times 3,300) about $3,146.
scenes.cap: Grid (20 arithmetic levels, $30 apart): buys at 2,970, 2,940 … 2,700 → average buy ≈ $2,835. Concentrated LP: converts USDC to ETH continuously on the way down at the Grid: sells at 3,030 … 3,300 → average ≈ $3,165. LP: sells ETH at √(3,000 × 3,300) ≈ $3,146.

lines: Price breaks below the range. What do the grid bot and the LP both hold?
scenes.sub: Answer: All, or nearly all, the base asset, bought on the way down. Both stop earning until price returns or you act.

lines: Who pays trading fees in each?
scenes.sub: Answer: The grid bot pays exchange fees. The LP earns fees from traders.

lines: Name one risk the LP has that the grid bot doesn't, and vice versa.
scenes.sub: Answer: LP: smart-contract/MEV/gas risk. Grid bot: exchange/counterparty risk.
